title: Pasta with potatoes, cavolo nero and beans

grandparents_cupboard.reason: Every ingredient is a plain staple: potatoes, dried pasta, cavolo nero, olive oil, garlic, tinned beans, hard cheese and lemon.

supermarket.reason: Cavolo nero, vegetarian hard cheese and tinned cannellini beans are everyday Tesco lines at ordinary prices.

basic_kitchen.reason: It needs only one large pan, a colander, a knife and a grater, and the technique is simple boiling and frying.

works.reason: 500g potatoes, 300g pasta, a tin of beans and 200g greens make a sensible amount for four, and 1.5cm cubes will cook alongside the pasta in 10 minutes.

honest_times.reason: Fifteen minutes is fair for peeling and cubing the potatoes, stripping the cavolo nero, slicing garlic and grating cheese, and twelve minutes matches the boil and the quick fry.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed item, including the chilli flakes, lemon and seasoning, is used in the steps, and nothing unlisted appears apart from water.

seasonal_feel.reason: Stored potatoes and garden cavolo nero suit a chilly March lunch, and the potatoes outweigh the pasta, so they are central to the dish.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are short, plain British English that a beginner could follow.

hearty_healthy.reason: It is a filling family lunch, with beans, greens and cheese balancing the starch.
